items.difficulty_reason: After basic curve regularity, group law and the supplied(c) no-single-simple-zero obstruction, author still constructs rational functions by line/vertical ratios inductively to characterize all finite-point principal complements and derives the converse. This concrete construction is the counted non-routine burden; it is not treated as a free Picard/Abel theorem.
items.statement_scope: Official Additional Exercises1 Q2(d), in full: for X=Spec(C[x,y]/(y^2-x(x-1)(x-2))), characterize principal opens; for a complement of distinct finite points P_i the supplied criterion is existence of strictly positive integers m_i with sum(m_i P_i)=O in the stated elliptic group law, and for every positive integer n there are n distinct points with nonprincipal complement. Empty and whole opens are trivial principal cases. Q2(c) is retained as necessary H1 context, not a separate count.

standard_prerequisites: Basic smooth affine-curve local regularity and zero/pole multiplicity
The chord-and-tangent abelian group law as explicitly recalled by the source
A rational function on this affine curve is regular iff it has no poles there, explicitly assumed by the author
Basic finite-torsion/countability facts for a complex elliptic curve; no free use of the target principal-divisor/group-sum criterion
source_caveats: The fixed source is the smooth affine complex cubic R=C[x,y]/(y^2-x(x-1)(x-2)), with identity infinity only on its projective completion. Removed points are distinct finite closed curve points; the group-relation multiplicities must be strictly positive integers.

Q2(c) is H1 context only: its no-single-simple-zero obstruction is used for the converse in(d). Q2(a,b), the generic-point/open-set setup, and the source chord-and-tangent law remain visible; only Q2(d) is counted.
The source group-law paragraph counts intersections with multiplicity, including tangent lines; later simple-zero wording for line/vertical functions is retained under that preceding convention.

The displayed induction omits a separate vertical-line branch when Q=P1+P2 is the identity infinity, where x_Q is undefined. Root judged this routine case bookkeeping; the author text is retained without a supplied replacement branch.

The source explains the n=1 countability/nontorsion example, then states the all-positive-n extension tersely. Root judged this routine inference bookkeeping; no expanded proof is attributed to the author.

The author explicitly assumes that a rational function on the affine curve is regular iff it has no poles there. The target positive-divisor/group-sum criterion is not assumed as a Picard/Abel prerequisite.
Both complete author PDFs are retained separately; surrounding Q1 and Q3 are not counted. Source license remains unknown; operator publication authorization is a separate record.
